patch_description: Instead of a sliding-window weighted average (which has fixed lag proportional to window size), I use a causal adaptive Kalman filter with a local linear trend state model (position + slope). The Kalman filter jointly estimates the level and slope of the signal, with online noise estimation: the measurement noise R is adapted from recent innovation statistics, and the process noise Q is adapted based on detected trend changes (innovation whiteness test). This gives near-zero phase lag (unlike windowed averages which lag by ~(W-1)/2), suppresses spurious slope reversals (the slope state acts as a regularized derivative that resists noise), and preserves genuine dynamics (adaptive Q lets the filter respond quickly to real trend changes). The output is then aligned to match the original sliding-window output length. This directly optimizes all four objectives: slope change minimization, lag minimization, tracking accuracy, and false reversal avoidance.
